S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

symptom.disease_info: Specific Phobia is characterized by a marked, persistent fear of a clearly discernible object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger posed, leading to avoidance or intense distress when confronted. The fear response is typically immediate and consistent, has lasted at least six months, and causes significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. Onset often follows a traumatic or distressing encounter with the feared stimulus or develops through observational learning or information transmission, and the course is usually chronic if untreated, though the fear may wax and wane with life circumstances. It is distinguished from social anxiety disorder, panic disorder, and PTSD by its narrow focus on a specific object or situation and the absence of broader social evaluation fears, spontaneous panic attacks in varied contexts, or re-experiencing of a traumatic event.

patient.personality: Oscar is disciplined, order‑oriented, and competitive, taking pride in efficiency and structure at work and in his carefully organized home life.
patient.stressor: About seven months ago, Oscar was working a late shift when an agitated customer abruptly knocked over a large store display that crashed down right beside his register, shattering glass and sending heavy boxes tumbling toward him while he was trapped in the narrow checkout lane. Already under pressure after his recent separation and pushing himself to earn a promotion, he felt intensely vulnerable and cornered in that confined workspace, and afterward he began to dread being assigned to that particular register lane and similar tight, boxed‑in spaces in the store. Over the following months, he quietly rearranged his schedule, traded shifts, and altered his usual routes through the store to avoid setups that reminded him of that incident, which slowed his checkout speed and drew criticism from supervisors who had always counted on his reliability. When he started turning down extra hours, skipping community soccer because the indoor facility felt too enclosed, and noticing his avoidance was jeopardizing his promotion prospects and income, he reluctantly agreed to see a psychiatrist at the urging of his sister, who saw how much this specific fear was disrupting his otherwise structured life.
patient.chief_complaint: “Whenever I get near that kind of tight checkout lane now, I get this rush of fear right away, like I have to get out of there immediately.”

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: Ever since that display crashed next to me, any time I see one of those narrow lanes with tall shelves on both sides, my chest tightens and I feel this strong, almost childlike fear that I’m trapped and something heavy is going to fall on me again, even though I know it’s just a normal checkout line.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: If my manager even points me toward that kind of tight register or I have to walk through a crowded, boxed‑in aisle, I get an instant jolt—my heart starts pounding, my palms sweat, and I just want to turn around and bolt out into the open part of the store.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: I go out of my way to switch to the wider lanes, take the long way around stock rooms and the indoor soccer field, and on the days I can’t avoid a cramped space at work I stand there stiff as a board, breathing fast and counting the minutes until I can get out, which slows me down and has gotten me in trouble with my supervisors.
